chapter: La Cigalle and settling in Paris
title: Leaving the Cigalle for Belgium and Germany; Al Levrat's band
summary: When Butler's band changed twice, Waters went to Belgium and to Germany; the third Cigalle band was led by Al Levrat, a Guadeloupean trombonist.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
So after you came out of the Cigalle the first time, in the mid '50's in Paris, is that when you went to Germany on your own?
Uh, say that again.
After you left, after Butler fell out with the Cigalle the first time, is that when you went to Germany for a while?

Yeah, I went - ah, I stayed, that happened twice. Not - it happened twice that way. The one time that the band changed the names I went to Belgium and the guy, and Jacques Butler asked me to come back. The other time he changed the names I went to Germany, I think the first time I went to Germany. And also went to Switzerland, but that was during the same period.
What kind of work did you do in Germany during this period - this is what, the '57, '56, that period?
Around '60, close to '60 at the James Paradise [?] -
Oh, so it was a long stretch of time with Butler in the middle '50's and Paris.
Yeah, yeah, we played quite a while there, see, when we went there the first time.
OK. Or before we -

The first time. See, it was three times, we had three different bands at - the first band was this little bebop band. And they had, they already made it - they didn't make it no more than six months and the man asked them to go back.
Right.
Then the Al Levrat, trombone player, he has a different little type of band -
How do you say that last name?
Al Levrat, Al Levrat -
L-E-V-A-T -
Not Levat, 'cause I get that, it's a drummer from New York here named Levat.
Uh huh.
But Levrat, V-R-A-T, is a Guadaloupean, from Guadaloupe.
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82 88
Uh huh. Could you spell that again, his last name?
Levat, L-E-V-R-A-T -
OK, gotcha.
Levrat, they call it A and R in French, so you say Levat.
